title: Fit the red gel frame in a 3 in fresnel before the lamp is struck
instruction: Put the red gel in the light.
context: A colour frame holding gel gets hot once an incandescent fixture has been on (University of Rochester lighting-lab notes). Gels must sit in the fixture's colour runners, not on the lens: gels placed directly on a hot lens can melt or burn (CINE-340 electrical and set safety). Pre-hang practice is to seat the framed gel in the runners while the lamp is still on the bench, before it is struck. This task is that last seating push: a 3.75 in red frame already in both runners of a 3 in inkie fresnel, 30 mm short of the stop, is pushed down until it sits. A blue frame in a gel box beside the lamp is not in the runners. The trial is cold and unpowered. IATSE lighting notes: more saturated gels absorb more heat and can melt. The fixture sits on its back, lens up, as when a lamp is gelled on the bench before it is hung.
setup: An Altman Lighting CAT #100 3 in Inky (black epoxy sandtex body, 3 in Pyrex stepped lens, plated-steel yoke, 510-B-style C-clamp, black focus thumbscrew and door knob) sits on the bench on its back, lens pointing up, as when a lamp is gelled before it is hung. It is unpowered; there is no lamp and no heat. Its colour-frame holders open along the barrel, with a stop. A 3.75 x 3.75 in (Altman 100-CFB size) aluminium colour frame already holds a pre-cut red Rosco (or LEE) gel and starts 30 mm short of the stop, already in both holders, offset so a sliver of the stepped lens stays visible at the start. The red face is a clear table-middle cue. A second, blue, frame lies in a shallow gel box beside the lamp and is not in the holders. All props are rigid and start on fixed marks.
scoring: As seen in the overhead video, the red frame is in both colour-frame holders. At the end, after 1 s at rest and with the gripper clear of the frame: 1.0 once the frame is on the stop (within 3 mm) and has been let go; 0.5 if the frame has been pushed at least 10 mm from the start but is still short of the stop, or if it is on the stop but has not been let go or is not yet still; 0 for the start pose itself (30 mm short, already in the holders) and for any path that never pushes. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Slide the red frame back 30 mm short of the stop, still in both holders. The blue frame stays in the gel box. The lamp is unpowered.
fidelity: Lamp and frames are rigid bodies dressed from the Altman 100: black sandtex body, plated yoke and C-clamp, black hardware, 3 in stepped lens and 3.75 in frame. The red frame is an X-slider in the holders (PhysX contactOffset is 4 mm; a free frame in real 3-5 mm runners is not used). The fixture sits on its back, lens up. The real 190 mm barrel would put the lens out of a straight-down grip, so the body is 70 mm — a REACH trade-off, not a hidden shrink. No lamp is struck; the trial is cold.
